speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT chest makes a full esophageal perforation less likely, but I must rule out other causes of severe chest pain and vomiting in this context. REQUEST TEST: Endoscopy

text: With normal imaging and endoscopy, I must consider non-perforative causes like Mallory-Weiss tear or severe gastritis. Have you observed any blood in your vomit or noticed black, tarry stools? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CBC and imaging, I need to rule out cardiac involvement or mediastinal pathology not seen on prior tests. REQUEST TEST: ECG REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal workup for perforation, cardiac, and bleeding causes, I suspect a musculoskeletal strain from the violent retching. Do you have tenderness over your chest wall muscles or ribs when I press on them? REQUEST TEST: Troponin

speaker: Doctor
text: With all major life-threatening causes ruled out by normal imaging, labs, and troponin levels, the clinical picture points to a musculoskeletal strain from the violent retching. DIAGNOSIS READY: Musculoskeletal chest pain secondary to forceful vomiting
